content.text: The evidence shows a sharp split: the tools handle version/tag/registry state reasonably, but none provides the complete “verify every external terminal state including assets and attestations” guarantee required here.

Research result for `REQ-DRAFT-RELEASE-RECOVERY` (current upstream docs/source checked 2026-09-16). “Confirmed” is direct upstream evidence; “limitation” means no matching guarantee was found in official docs/source after targeted search.

| Tool | Canonical identity / tags | PR approval → execution | Fixed vs independent | Registry publication ownership | Assets / attestations | Idempotency & recovery | Dry-run / staging |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Changesets | **Confirmed:** monorepo tags are per package: `pkg-name@version`; single-package uses `vversion`. [CLI docs](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/docs/command-line-options.md#git-tag) | **Confirmed:** action creates/updates a “Version Packages” PR while changesets exist; after merge it runs configured publish script. This is a workflow convention, not an approval-state model. [action README](https://github.com/changesets/action) | **Confirmed:** default independent; `fixed` groups version/publish every member together; `linked` only aligns members actually released. [linked-package docs](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/docs/linked-packages.md) | **Confirmed:** `changeset publish` owns npm/pnpm publication and determines an unpublished plan; custom action `publish-script` can replace it. [publish source](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/packages/cli/src/commands/publish/index.ts#L103-L147) | **Limitation:** action can create GitHub releases/tags, but no upstream support found for binary construction/upload, checksums, or GitHub artifact attestations. | **Confirmed:** CLI computes unpublished releases; source explicitly accepts `failed:already-published`, creates tags for successful publishes, reports existing tags, and exits nonzero on hard failures. [publish source](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/packages/cli/src/commands/publish/index.ts#L249-L387). **Risk:** action explicitly says custom publishing must itself handle versions already published after a successful prior run. [action README](https://github.com/changesets/action) | **Confirmed:** snapshot versions/dist-tags are intended for temporary test publishing. [CLI docs](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/docs/command-line-options.md). **Limitation:** no full end-to-end dry-run that models GitHub release/assets/attestation execution. |
| Knope | **Confirmed:** package tags are `vX.Y.Z` for one package and `<package>/vX.Y.Z` for multi-package; one GitHub release per package. [release step](https://knope.tech/reference/config-file/steps/release/), [monorepo tutorial](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-multiple-packages/) | **Confirmed:** documented standard flow is a manually/workflow-dispatched `knope release` that mutates, commits/pushes, then releases. Preview PRs exist as a recipe, but no native “merged approved release PR automatically authorizes execution” boundary was found. [basic tutorial](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-basic-projects/) | **Confirmed:** multi-package tutorial says packages update independently; a package may cover multiple registry formats/files. [tutorial](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-multiple-packages/) | **Confirmed:** release workflow itself handles version/changelog/tag/forge release; registry publication is a separately configured workflow command, rather than a protected first-class transaction. The docs show arbitrary `Command` steps between prepare/release. [release step](https://knope.tech/reference/config-file/steps/release/) | **Confirmed:** release assets supported; it creates a draft release, uploads assets serially, then publishes it. [release assets](https://knope.tech/reference/config-file/steps/release/#release-assets). **Limitation:** no upstream evidence of checksum creation or artifact attestation support. | **Confirmed contradiction:** an existing forge release is documented as a conflict/failure, not a satisfied verified result. [errors](https://knope.tech/reference/config-file/steps/release/#errors). No fresh-runner convergent recovery guarantee found. | **Confirmed:** `knope release --dry-run` previews file updates, git commands, and GitHub release; docs say dry-run works with any Knope command. [tutorial](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-basic-projects/). **Limitation:** no isolated-registry/repository rehearsal model found. |
| Nx Release | **Confirmed:** fixed default tag `v{version}`; independent default `{projectName}@{version}`; custom tag patterns permitted. [Nx config reference](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/nx-json#release-tag) | **Confirmed:** docs’ primary CI pattern is local `nx release --skip-publish` then tag-triggered publish workflow; it is not release-PR approval execution. [publish in CI/CD](https://nx.dev/docs/guides/nx-release/publish-in-ci-cd) | **Confirmed:** fixed is default and requires all group projects version together; independent is supported. [release groups](https://nx.dev/docs/guides/nx-release/release-groups) | **Confirmed:** `nx release publish` runs a per-project `nx-release-publish` executor; docs support npm, Cargo/crates.io, Docker, and custom registries. [overview](https://nx.dev/docs/features/manage-releases), [CI guide](https://nx.dev/docs/guides/nx-release/publish-in-ci-cd). | **Confirmed:** GitHub Releases receive generated changelog content. [GitHub release guide](https://nx.dev/docs/kb/automate-github-releases). **Limitation:** no native binary asset/checksum/attestation flow found; these require additional workflow steps. | **Confirmed:** npm flow uses `npm view` to skip existing published versions, explicitly allowing re-running the same publish action without negative effects. [npm guide](https://nx.dev/docs/kb/release-npm-packages#future-releases). **Risk:** that documented guarantee is npm-specific; executor-level exit results are aggregated, but no cross-registry/assets final verification contract is documented. [source](https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/packages/nx/src/command-line/release/publish.ts#L41-L52) | **Confirmed:** `nx release --dry-run` previews and avoids updating files/creating releases; dry-run reaches publish executors via `NX_DRY_RUN`. [overview](https://nx.dev/docs/features/manage-releases), [source](https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/packages/nx/src/command-line/release/publish.ts#L219-L225). **Limitation:** preview is not an isolated rehearsal with credential/registry substitutes. |
| Release Please | **Confirmed:** manifest mode records version by package; default tag is `<component>-v<version>`, configurable to `v<version>` via `include-component-in-tag: false`. [manifest docs](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/manifest-releaser.md#subsequent-versions) | **Confirmed:** it creates/updates a release PR; after merge, GitHub release/tag creation occurs. It explicitly warns not to merge two release PRs before release execution. [CLI docs](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/cli.md), [manifest docs](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/manifest-releaser.md) | **Confirmed:** manifest supports many configured packages, but default release behavior is package/component oriented; Rust monorepo dependency updates require the cargo-workspace plugin. [manifest docs](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/manifest-releaser.md#plugins) **Limitation:** no direct fixed lockstep-release-group guarantee comparable to Nx’s fixed groups found. | **Confirmed:** it deliberately does not publish packages; official Lerna example says release-please has incremented/tagged and a separate `lerna publish from-package` does npm publication. [manifest docs](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/manifest-releaser.md#using-with-github-actions-and-lerna) | **Confirmed:** official action example uses a separate `gh release upload` step for an artifact. [action README](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please-action#attaching-artifacts-to-releases). **Limitation:** no native multi-target binaries, checksums, or GitHub artifact attestations. | **Confirmed:** GitHub release creation is explicitly non-transactional, but safely rerunnable to finish releases that failed. [CLI docs](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/cli.md#create-a-manifest-release-deprecated). **Risk:** this covers GitHub releases/tags, not external publication or uploaded-asset verification. | **Confirmed:** `github-release` / manifest-release has `--dry-run`; draft releases are supported. [CLI docs](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/cli.md). **Limitation:** no documented substitute-registry/repository rehearsal. |

Transferable patterns:

- Adopt a single fixed release group and one canonical tag. Nx proves the useful mechanics: fixed membership means no subset release, one tag per coordinated release, and custom tag patterns can express `callisto@X.Y.Z`.
- Adopt manifest/plan-derived recovery: Changesets’ “unpublished plan” and Nx’s explicit registry lookup before re-publishing are the strongest directly relevant ideas. Strengthen them: treat an existing item as satisfied only after exact external verification, not merely an “already exists” response.
- Separate preparation/review from execution as Release Please does, but bind execution to the immutable reviewed PR commit/plan. Release Please’s explicit non-transactionality demonstrates why rerun logic must be intentional.
- Use Knope’s draft-release → upload-all-assets → publish ordering for public GitHub visibility, but add post-upload checksum and attestation verification before declaring completion.
- Preserve dry-run previews, but reject treating them as rehearsal evidence. None of the four provides the requirement’s isolated end-to-end interruption/fresh-runner recovery exercise.

Anti-patterns / unresolved risks:

- Per-package tags/releases (Changesets, Knope defaults, Release Please manifest) conflict with the required single product identity.
- Existing-release-as-conflict (Knope) cannot meet convergent recovery.
- “Publication succeeded” without a final external read-back is insufficient; no examined tool guarantees verification of registry metadata, tag target, GitHub release, every asset checksum, and every attestation as one terminal success condition.
- Workflow labels/output flags are not a durable execution-state machine. No examined tool documents a persistent, runner-independent operation journal keyed to an immutable release plan.
